answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work. Each agent must first complete small attested tasks on a shared ledger, earning a trust score that grows only slowly — like a knoll that rises over many seasons, standing cannot be faked overnight. New identities begin at dawn with zero weight, while an onyx ledger of proven sock-puppets is published for all peers to refuse. Influence then tracks history, not headcount.
